Using zero-authentication NASA POWER API (MERRA-2) time-series data alongside live NASA GIBS (MODIS Terra) satellite imagery, the app computes Ordinary Least Squares decadal slopes, Pearson cross-correlation (rrr), and two-tailed Student's t-tests (p < 0.05$) in real time.This matters because most climate tools examine isolated locations without proving statistical significance. details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TeleConnection: NASA Earth Trend Detective is an interactive geospatial and statistical web application built to uncover planetary climate dipoles ("environmental seesaws") pairs of regions across Earth experiencing statistically opposite long-term trends over a 20-year period (2005–2024). Users click any two points on an interactive satellite map (or launch curated dipole presets such as Indus Basin vs. Horn of Africa or California Megadrought vs. US Northeast Wetting) and select an Earth-system variable: 2-Meter Temperature (T2M), Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), Surface Soil Wetness (GWETTOP), or All-Sky Shortwave Solar Irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).

In real time, the platform queries 20 years of NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 assimilation) monthly records, filters missing-value sentinels, aggregates annual averages in standardized SI units, and runs an in-browser statistical engine performing Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression, Pearson cross-correlation (rrr), and a two-tailed Student's t-test (p-value). Simultaneously, it streams NASA GIBS (MODIS Terra) satellite imagery onto the map with a 2005–2024 temporal slider so users can visually inspect surface changes alongside mathematical proof of divergence, then publish verified findings to a Community Detective Archive.

What benefits does it have, and what is the intended impact?

  • Democratizes Climate Telemetry: Eliminates the need for researchers, students, and citizens to download massive multi-gigabyte NetCDF/HDF5 files or write custom Python pipelines just to test regional climate relationships.
  • Prevents False-Positive Trend Claims: By enforcing a strict p<0.05p < 0.05p<0.05 statistical significance threshold alongside decadal slope calculations, the tool distinguishes genuine climate divergence from random year-to-year weather noise.
  • Intended Impact: Empower global citizens, educators, and climate analysts to collaboratively map interconnected regional anomalies—helping communities understand how drying, warming, or solar shifts in one region mirror opposite trends elsewhere on Earth.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • NASA Open Data APIs:
    • NASA POWER API (power.larc.nasa.gov): Zero-authentication 20-year monthly MERRA-2 time-series telemetry (2005–2024).
    • NASA GIBS WMTS (gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov): Live satellite map tile streaming (MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor and MODIS_Terra_Aerosol).
  • Frontend & Visualization Stack: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion (kinetic transitions), Leaflet / React-Leaflet (geospatial mapping & geodesic arcs), and Recharts (dual-series regression visualization).
  • Statistical Engine & Storage: Custom TypeScript OLS linear regression, Pearson correlation, and Student's ttt-distribution inference module (src/utils/earthStats.ts), paired with client-side localStorage persistence and optional Supabase PostgreSQL integration for the Community Detective Archive.
  • Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, and Vercel.

How is the project creative? Most climate dashboards only display isolated single-city line charts. TeleConnection flips that paradigm by treating Earth as a paired, interconnected system visually connecting two distant regions with a live geodesic arc on real NASA satellite imagery while plotting their opposing "X-shaped" regression trendlines side by side. Combining an editorial, high-contrast mission-control interface with instant statistical hypothesis testing transforms raw Earth-observation data into an intuitive "detective" workflow.

What factors were considered during development?

  • Zero-Friction Accessibility: Selected zero-authentication NASA APIs (NASA POWER and NASA GIBS) so any judge or user anywhere in the world can run live queries immediately without API-key bottlenecks or server latency.
  • Scientific & SI Unit Rigor: Enforced standardized SI and derived physical units (°C/decade, mm/day, kW-hr/m²/day, and Haversine geodesic distance in km) while filtering out NASA's -999 sentinel values and month-13 summary keys so statistical outputs remain accurate.
  • Map & Data Edge Cases: Configured maxNativeZoom tile scaling on NASA GIBS layers to prevent blank tiles at high zoom levels and built graceful handling for ocean coordinates where land-surface parameters are unavailable.
